title: a FETCH result's tuples freed by a failed spill and freed again when its portal drops -- tuplestore double free
consumer: FETCH BACKWARD ALL into the unnamed portal's tuplestore, then ROLLBACK
live_proof: measured 2026-10-29 on p13: PostgreSQL 17.5 (the port's tarball, sha256 fcb7ab38...28d8), configured --enable-debug CFLAGS='-O1 -g' CPPFLAGS=-DUSE_VALGRIND (no cassert, as the port), trigger.sql through `postgres --single` under Valgrind 3.26 with src/tools/valgrind.supp: one error, 'Invalid free()' at pfree (mcxt.c:1531) by tuplestore_end (tuplestore.c:462) by PortalDrop (portalmem.c:585) by CreatePortal (portalmem.c:193) by exec_simple_query -- the report's own backtrace, on the ROLLBACK. control.sql on the same build: no error. Natively the second pfree is silent: the backend completes and answers `survived`, as upstream's commit message says of v16 and v17 ("the specific test case submitted failed to fail there").
fidelity: real server, core. Upstream bug #19438's own reproducer with MOVE ALL for the forward FETCH ALL whose output the report discarded. The same defect is ../../mmgr-repros/00_1f5b6a5e5d_tuplestore_double_free as a C program against the real memory contexts; this one reaches it in the whole backend, and the two must not be counted twice.
nested_why: the freed tuples are palloc chunks in the portal's aset context: the spill's pfree and the second one both stay inside an aset block that malloc never sees freed
fault_sites_why: Valgrind with PostgreSQL's own mempool annotations (USE_VALGRIND) on the host, recorded before any Capstone arm ran: the invalid free is at pfree (mcxt.c:1531) called from tuplestore_end (tuplestore.c:462). A fault in another function counts through control.sql.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, PostgreSQL's contexts stock (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng): a fault after the trigger started that its control.sql or a justified fault_sites ties to the defect, or the trigger completes and this arm did not see it

virtual-pg-pools.oracle: virtual profile with the memory-context port's patch 0003: every palloc chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE) (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng-pg-pools): as virtual-malloc

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes: both frees are inside an aset block, which libc's revocation never sees freed, so the platform has nothing to revoke

status: live at the pin, measured on the host under Valgrind (2026-10-29); first Capstone reading in results/2026-10-29-virtual, beside the corpus's verdict_bundles and not derived into this file: virtual-malloc MISSED, virtual-pg-pools CAUGHT (cause 25 in SubletRelease, by control). cheribsd-revocation has not run it
